crm_note.headline: Arjun Nair completed the second round at Lumenfold Research (three sessions); concerned about an equity-heavy package with a lower base
crm_note.how_it_went: Arjun described the afternoon as "good, I think". He felt shaky on the checkpointing restart question, where he had forgotten data loader state until Oren asked, and on a back-of-the-envelope checkpoint write estimate he got wrong first time before getting there slowly. He felt solid on the parallelism questions and said he enjoyed the eval contamination question.

rounds.round: Session 1: systems design with Oren (pre-training infra team)
asked: Design checkpointing for a training run across a few thousand GPUs: how often to save, how to avoid stalling the job while writing, what happens when a node dies mid-save
How long it takes to restart and get back to the same step
Whether the data loader state is in the checkpoint
Back-of-the-envelope estimate of checkpoint write time for a given model size and bandwidth
rounds.candidate_view: He proposed async checkpointing to host memory with background writes, sharded state so each rank writes its own piece, and keeping the last two good checkpoints. He had forgotten the data loader state until Oren asked; he recovered but felt Oren noticed. He did the write-time arithmetic wrong first time and got there slowly. He named both as the parts that felt shaky.

asked: What he would check on a loss curve with spikes
When to use FSDP versus tensor parallel, and the communication cost of each
rounds.candidate_view: He went through learning rate warmup, bad batches, fp16 overflow, attention logits blowing up and gradient norm, and said Hana liked that he asked for the gradient norm plot before guessing. He said he was solid on parallelism, as it is what he does every day at Whitfenn.

rounds.round: Session 3: research deep dive with Marta (research lead)
rounds.format: Research deep dive on his data mixing paper
asked: Why he chose a particular ablation and not another
Whether the result would hold at bigger scale
How he would know a benchmark had leaked into the training data (eval contamination)
rounds.candidate_view: He said he enjoyed the eval contamination question.

compensation.expectation: Base around £175k (given to the Lumenfold recruiter at the end of the day)
compensation.notes: Lumenfold's recruiter said equity is options with a four-year vest and a one-year cliff, and the valuation would be explained at offer stage. Arjun has a mortgage and is unsure about the role if the base is lower and the package is mostly equity. Priya to get the base range firmed up before he goes further.

crm_note.notice_and_non_compete: Eight weeks' notice, no non-compete (Whitfenn does not use them).
competing_processes: Big tech offer that he is probably going to turn down
risks: Equity-heavy package: Arjun said that if the base is lower and the package is mostly equity, he is not sure about the role, as he has a mortgage. The base range needs firming up before the final stage.

next_actions.action: Get the base salary range for the role firmed up with Lumenfold by phone before Arjun goes further in the process
Final stage (values and team chat, plus a call with the head of infra) timing
next_actions.due: a week or so (said on the call)

candidate.subject: Lumenfold Research: next steps
candidate.body:
Hi Arjun,

Thank you for the call today and for talking me through the three sessions at Lumenfold.

I have noted your expectation of a base around £175k, your eight-week notice period with no non-compete, and that equity at Lumenfold is options with a four-year vest and a one-year cliff.

I have also noted your point about the equity and your mortgage. Before you go any further in the process, I will get the base salary range firmed up with Lumenfold so you are not surprised at offer stage.

I will call you on Friday.

Best wishes,
Priya

process.format: Design problem on checkpointing for a large training run. The second round is three interviews across a full afternoon.
process.who: Oren, from the pre-training infra team
process.what_they_look_for: He pushed on the restart side: how long it takes to get back to the same step, and whether the data loader state is in the checkpoint. He also asked for a back-of-the-envelope estimate of checkpoint write time.

process.round: Second round, part 2: debugging and parallelism
process.format: Debugging a loss curve with spikes, then questions on parallelism
process.what_they_look_for: She liked a request for the gradient norm plot before any guessing at the cause.

process.round: Second round, part 3: research deep dive
process.format: Deep dive on one of your own papers, picked by the interviewer, plus a question on eval contamination
process.what_they_look_for: She goes deep into the reasoning behind your experimental choices and whether the results would hold at bigger scale.

process.format: Values and team chat, plus a call with the head of infra
process.who: Head of infra; others not discussed

examples: Design the checkpointing for a training run across a few thousand GPUs: how often you save, how you avoid stalling the whole job while you write, and what happens when a node dies mid-save.
How long does it take to get back to the same step on restart?
Is the data loader state in the checkpoint?
Estimate, back of the envelope, how long a checkpoint write takes for a given model size and bandwidth.
A loss curve with spikes: what would you check?
When would you use FSDP versus tensor parallel, and what is the communication cost of each?

question_themes.theme: Deep dive on your own research
examples: Why that ablation, and why not this one?
Would the result hold at bigger scale?
How would you know a benchmark had leaked into the training data?

went_well: On the loss spikes question, asking for the gradient norm plot before guessing at a cause was something Hana liked.
tripped_people_up: On checkpointing, Oren pushed on restart: the time to get back to the same step, and whether data loader state is in the checkpoint. Data loader state was missed until he asked, and he noticed.
The back-of-the-envelope estimate of checkpoint write time for a given model size and bandwidth came out wrong the first time. The right answer was reached, but slowly.
advice: In checkpointing design, cover restart as fully as saving: say how quickly the job gets back to the same step, and include data loader state in what gets checkpointed.
Practise quick estimates of checkpoint write time from model size and bandwidth so the arithmetic is right first time.
On debugging questions, ask for diagnostics such as the gradient norm plot before guessing at causes.
Be ready to explain the reasoning behind each ablation in your papers, which alternatives you did not run, and whether the results would hold at larger scale.
Prepare a clear answer on how you would detect a benchmark leaking into the training data.
logistics: The second round is three interviews across a full afternoon.
The final stage is a values and team chat plus a call with the head of infra. The firm gave the timing for next steps after the second round as a week or so.
Equity is options with a four-year vest and a one-year cliff. The valuation is explained at offer stage.
